# What the grader accepts

`qccd.workspace.evaluator.grade(release, bundle)` is the one grader: the official server, `qccd grade <bundle>` and `qccd submit --local` all call it.

## Policy constants

- Stage statuses: `passed`, `failed`, `partial`, `skipped`, `unsupported`, `timeout`, `cancelled`, `internal_error`
- The board's rule set when its release names none: `standard`
- Rules the rules stage may report as skipped: R10, R7b, R9
- Rules the rules stage may report as partial: C8, R15
- Any other skipped or partial rule makes the rules stage `partial`, so the entry is not eligible.

## How the rules stage judges each board rule

Read off the code by running the stage's two checkers on an empty programme: `qccd.verify` (always) and the rule language (only when the board's release names a set). A rule the verifier does not report and the language does not reach is not judged by this stage.

### `c2lr` boards (4)

| Rule | Title | Rules stage |
|---|---|---|
| [C1](https://qccd.academy/rules/#C1) | A leg holds one crystal, or two between an enter and its exit | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [C2](https://qccd.academy/rules/#C2) | A C2LR step's only per-leg choice is its direction bit | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [C3](https://qccd.academy/rules/#C3) | Horizontal and vertical legs choose independently | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [C4](https://qccd.academy/rules/#C4) | A step is C2LR, one shared waveform, C2LR back | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [C5](https://qccd.academy/rules/#C5) | Every crystal ends a step at a leg centre | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [C6](https://qccd.academy/rules/#C6) | A step pairs legs by the device's matching | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [C7](https://qccd.academy/rules/#C7) | No crystal ends a step in a junction | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |

| [C10](https://qccd.academy/rules/#C10) | Control is shared signals plus one input and one switch per leg | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |

| [R1](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R1) | A site holds at most its capacity | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [R2](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R2) | A junction holds one ion at a time | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [R3](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R3) | A rail carries at most its capacity | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [R4](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R4) | Every transport step uses a movement the device declares | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [R4b](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R4b) | A step either moves ions or gates them, never both | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [R4d](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R4d) | The control channels can drive every transport step | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [R5](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R5) | No two ions pass each other on a rail in one step | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [R6](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R6) | Each operation runs only where the site is equipped for it | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [R6b](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R6b) | A two-ion gate acts on two ions standing in one site | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |

| [R7b](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R7b) | A gate zone stays within its heat duty cycle | may be skipped (qccd.verify skips it: no per-zone duty-cycle budget is declared by any architecture yet) |

| [R8](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R8) | An ion does one thing at a time | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |

| [R19](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R19) | A junction joins at most max_junction_degree() rails | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [R20](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R20) | Rails meet at a wide enough angle | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [R21](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R21) | Rails lie in a plane | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [R22](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R22) | A transport step is one waveform | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [R23](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R23) | A junction is crossed, not rested on | must pass (qccd.verify and the rule language) |
| [R24](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R24) | Every two-qubit gate of the circuit is performed, and no other | not judged by the rules stage: the rule language gets no circuit there, so it does not apply; only the certificate stages speak to it |
| [R25](https://qccd.academy/rules/#R25) | Each qubit's operations keep the circuit's order | not judged by the rules stage: the rule language gets no circuit there, so it does not apply; only the certificate stages speak to it |

## What the probe found

- surface device: qccd.verify reports 28 rule ids (R1 R10 R11 R12 R13 R14 R15 R16 R17 R18 R19 R2 R20 R21 R22 R23 R3 R4 R4b R4d R5 R6 R6b R7 R7b R7c R8 R9); skips R10, R7b, R9; partial R15; rule-language rules that need the circuit: R24, R25
- c2lr device: qccd.verify reports 38 rule ids (C1 C10 C2 C3 C4 C5 C6 C7 C8 C9 R1 R10 R11 R12 R13 R14 R15 R16 R17 R18 R19 R2 R20 R21 R22 R23 R3 R4 R4b R4d R5 R6 R6b R7 R7b R7c R8 R9); skips R10, R7b, R9; partial C8, R15; rule-language rules that need the circuit: R24, R25

## The stages, in the evaluator's own words

```
The evaluator: `grade(trusted_task_release, bundle, profile) -> report`.

One contract, independent of transport: the local service, the CLI and the official
worker all call `grade`.  It reuses the toolchain rather than restating it -- the loader
(`Architecture.from_json`), the replay and the 27 rules (`qccd.verify.verify`), the
trusted checker input builder (`Compiler/bridge/mk_qcheck_input.py`), the proved Lean
checker (`qcheck`) and the semantic checker (`Compiler/bridge/check_cert.py`, whose
`check_binding` is also the certificate binding).

WHAT A PASSING REFERENCE REPORT ESTABLISHES, stage by stage (and nothing more):

  bundle               every file hashes to its manifest digest; the manifest names THIS task
                       release (id and digest); no stray or unknown members.
  device               the device loads under the architecture schema and structure checks.
  physics_lock         the device is scored with the release's physics.json: its own number is
                       used only where the release has none (`tasks.scored_device`), and every
                       such number is listed (`added`), as is every number of its own that was
                       not used (`ignored`); the budget is the release's.
  program              the final program is a well-formed TSIR within the release limits.
  rules                replaying the final program on the device under the task model, every
                       rule of the entry's rule set passes: the board's, or the set the bundle
                       declares (`rules.json`, checked in the rule language,
                       `qccd.ruleset.declared`).  The board's set is `standard`, checked by
                       `qccd.verify`, unless the release declares one (`rules`: the C2LR boards'
                       `c2lr`), which is checked in the rule language as well, the replay taking
                       its parameters.  The board's rules are checked either way, so the report
                       says which of them the entry keeps.  Rules the replay cannot check are
                       listed as skipped with the reason, and only the release's
                       `allowed_skips` may be skipped.
  correspondence       the final program is the certified program with only the release's
                       allowed transformations applied (inserted `cool` instructions),
                       instruction by instruction, ids included.
  certificate_binding  the certificate's circuit is the trusted task circuit, op for op
                       (`check_cert.check_binding`: a 1- or 2-qubit op as itself, a
                       composite as a run of ops whose product is its defining unitary),
                       with the task's qubit count and a one-to-one qubit map; its gate
                       witnesses name instructions of the certified program that carry the
                       same operation stamps (`qccd.ir.source_map`).
  lean_certificate     the proved Lean checker accepts the certificate against facts it
                       re-derives from the SUBMITTED device (`check_sound`).
  semantics            O1 (transport replay of the certificate) and O2 (the stabilizer
                       tableau composed from the certified program's emitted pulses equals
                       the tableau of the TRUSTED circuit) both hold, and no op is
                       unrealised.  Outside the Clifford fragment O2 is `partial`.
  ler                  (memory boards only: a release with a `qec` block) the final program,
                       read through the certificate's qubit->ion map as the release's memory
                       experiment, has detectors and observables that are deterministic with
                       the circuit's parity; its logical error rate under the release's noise
                       model and sampling budget is measured (qccd.qec.evaluate_memory).  The
                       LER is a Monte Carlo estimate with a fixed seed: the same machine gives
                       the same number, another machine may differ within its interval.
  metrics              the leaderboard numbers, from `metrics.compute_metrics` (and, on a memory
                       board, `ler` and `ler_per_round` from the stage above).

It does NOT establish physical realisability beyond the task's model: the rules and the
physics tables are the model.  The certificate's transport is compared with the final
program's: check_cert.py replays both and requires each ion's moves (and every rotation)
to be the same, in order (`o1_transport`, which feeds O1); co-location of the program's
own gates is R6b of the replay, and the semantic link is O2 through the certificate's
qubit->ion map.

Eligibility is decided by the release's policy: every required check `passed`, under the
`reference` profile.  A skipped, unsupported, partial, timed-out or cancelled required
check is never eligible -- absence of a failure is not a pass.

`conformance` says how an eligible entry stands to the BOARD: whether it keeps every rule of
the board's set with the board's physics (`board`), and if not, which rules it breaks, what its
declared set drops, replaces and adds, and which physics numbers are its own.  A leaderboard
ranks the entries that conform unless a reader asks for every entry (the user's decision of
2026-10-29: the board's rules first, the others a filter away).
```

## The verifier's one-line statements (`qccd.verify.rules.RULE_STATEMENTS`)

These are the verifier's own summaries. Where one reads differently from the catalogue, the catalogue (`rules.md`) is the rule.

| Rule | Statement |
|---|---|
| R1 | occupancy(site) <= site.capacity at every instant |
| R2 | at most one ion occupies any junction at any instant |
| R3 | at most segment.capacity ions occupy any shuttling segment |
| R4 | at most max_simd_classes_per_cycle classes active; a class fixes (type, direction); participation is variadic |
| R4b | intra-trap and inter-trap transport never overlap in time |
| R4d | a cycle must be drivable by the declared control channels: one channel carries one waveform, and opting out needs a per-site switch |
| R5 | no two ions exchange positions along one segment in a single step |
| R6 | gate / measure / cool only where the zone type has the capability |
| R6b | a 2Q gate acts only on ions co-located in the same gate zone |
| R7 | a 2Q gate requires both ions' n-bar <= ms_gate.max_quanta |
| R7b | per-gate-zone thermal duty-cycle budget, not just instantaneous occupancy |
| R7c | cooling is mandatory under broadcast wiring |
| R8 | the ion->site map is a bijection over time outside explicit load/unload |
| R9 | claimed steps/cost/duration/quanta equal the replayed values |
| R10 | the compiled program implements the input circuit |
| R11 | shuttling is unidirectional; a trap connects to <= 2 shuttling paths |
| R12 | intra-trap parallelism = 1; inter-trap parallelism unconstrained |
| R13 | 2Q gate time degrades sharply above ~15 ions per trap |
| R14 | an ion must be at a trap edge to split; getting there costs a 3-CX swap |
| R15 | quanta compose with an interference term, not additively |
| R16 | 2Q gate error is a function of accumulated n-bar at gate time |
| R17 | anomalous heating accrues with elapsed time whether or not an ion moves |
| R18 | a node is a junction only if three or more trap axes meet at it |
| R19 | a junction joins at most max_junction_degree rails (6 unless the document declares fewer) |
| R20 | two rails meeting at a node subtend at least min_rail_angle_deg (60 degrees) |
| R21 | rails are planar: a rail meets only the nodes it ends at, and rails cross only at a shared node |
| R22 | one transport cycle is one waveform: every moving ion performs the same motion; a site may only opt out |
| R23 | a junction is crossed, not rested on: no ion ends a cycle where three or more rails meet while the traps off the junctions have room, unless a conveyor carries it there |
